We have long warned everyone not to disclose sensitive personal information in AI chatbot conversations, because most companies use these conversations as training data. But now, there is an even more serious reason to do so.

Over the weekend, the situation worsened, as a Reddit user discovered that it was possible to retrieve some Claude AI chat records through a simple Google search...

Claude Chat Content Leak

Claude offers a sharing feature that lets you share chat conversations with colleagues, friends, or family. The chatbot generates a link that you can send to one or more recipients, and Claude implicitly assures you that even people who know the URL cannot view the conversation.

The problem is that Reddit users discovered that you don't actually need the link to view the conversation. You can find it simply through a Google search, whether by using specific search terms or by asking Google directly to display all conversations shared in this way. BBC News reported:

You basically just need to tell Google to search the directory used for sharing Claude conversations (i.e., site:claude.ai/share), and that's it.

As you might expect, some of the chat conversations were completely absurd—for example, someone asking why the record industry was hiding the fact that most of Jay-Z's albums were actually co-written by birds. But some conversations contain extremely sensitive information, such as verbatim transcripts of private conversations, a lawyer asking whether they needed to self-report a breach of conduct, and a user asking for help setting up a cryptocurrency wallet and inadvertently revealing their private key in the process.

Anthropic is still trying to claim this is not a problem.

In fact, of course it is a very serious problem, because this is completely not what users expected. Worse still, according to Wired's report, the root cause of the problem appears to be extreme negligence.

Prior to this, there were already reports that Claude Cowork was able to escape its sandbox environment and gain full access to all files on Mac.

How to Protect Yourself

The issue appears to have been at least partially resolved, as previously searchable results are now dead links, but given that this feature relies on the principle of "security by obscurity," I still recommend everyone avoid using the sharing feature.

I also recommend deleting all previously shared conversations. You can do so by going to "Settings > Privacy > Shared Conversations > Manage."

Once Again Proving the Superiority of Apple's Approach

Apple's Apple Intelligence and the new Siri adopt a three-tier architecture for privacy protection:

  • When feasible, AI processing is done on-device.
  • The first fallback is to use Apple's own Private Cloud Compute (PCC) servers.
  • The final option is to use a Gemini model with equivalent PCC safeguards.

The extremely sophisticated PCC architecture means that neither Apple nor Google can absolutely access any data, nor will any data be retained. The security architecture designed by Apple also allows independent security researchers to verify that its claims are true.
